forbidden_behaviors: LLM or user payload widens tenant, user, role, run, or trace identity.
Replay omits a safe trusted-context projection proof for the run.
Raw request or trusted-context payload is persisted instead of safe refs and reason codes.

decision_assertions.asserts: Replay-safe node/run payloads carry trusted replay context projection refs without accepting LLM or user-payload identity overrides.
Trace and replay API projections remain owner/admin-only and do not authorize from requested_by.user.merchant_id.

rows.notes: Uses existing run and node replay events; Phase 35 tests assert payload/projection content rather than adding a dedicated context event type.

forbidden_behaviors: Model confidence directly authorizes action routing.
Effective route omits policy-owner and reason-code trace.
High-risk/action intent calibration is reported as production-ready without release-gate evidence.

decision_assertions.asserts: Effective intent route is projected with policy owner, reason codes, risk/operation hints, and release-gate status without using LLM output as authority.
Release gate artifacts distinguish statistical readiness from deterministic Phase 35 dev-contract blockers.

rows.notes: Intent policy coverage uses the existing contextual-intent node event plus trace/eval projections; broad statistical expansion remains a release-gate artifact.

forbidden_behaviors: Stale, wrong-thread, wrong-tenant, or incompatible inherited slots pass the slot gate.
Current-turn explicit slots are overwritten by untrusted memory or model output.
Missing required slots route into action-bound paths without clarification.

decision_assertions.asserts: Slot inheritance/rejection decisions include source, freshness, missing-slot, stale, and incompatible reason codes.

rows.notes: Slot policy remains trace-projection coverage over the existing node event; no ad hoc slot replay event is introduced.

forbidden_behaviors: Memory context satisfies policy evidence, current business fact, approval, action, or replay authority.
Wrong-thread, wrong-user, wrong-tenant, stale, or incompatible memory enters prompt or trace projections.
Memory load omits scope/freshness/rejection reason codes.

decision_assertions.asserts: Memory load projection records tenant/thread/user scope, authority_class=contextual_only, accepted refs, and rejection reason codes.

rows.notes: Memory load coverage is carried by target trace projection and node completion payload contracts.

forbidden_behaviors: Raw memory content, PII, or private reasoning enters replay payloads.
Skipped or review-required memory candidates are reported as published memory.
Memory write quality metrics are claimed without monitoring status semantics.

decision_assertions.asserts: Memory write lifecycle events expose only status refs, counts, policy versions, and safe reason codes.
Monitoring artifact tracks memory write quality as pending/sample-only when production telemetry is unavailable.

rows.notes: Memory write lifecycle events already exist; Phase 35 gates assert safe payloads and monitoring schema semantics.

forbidden_behaviors: Planner sees raw tool descriptors, adapters, required_permission internals, or side-effect capability details.
Hidden tool decisions omit stable denial reason codes.
Tool visibility is treated as runtime authorization.

decision_assertions.asserts: Tool visibility event payload contains prompt-safe ToolView fields, decision, reason codes, and policy version only.

rows.notes: Uses existing tool policy visibility event introduced before Phase 35.

forbidden_behaviors: Visible tools are automatically allowed at runtime without scope, permission, side-effect, or schema checks.
Denied runtime auth leaks raw identifiers or internal permission reasons.
Runtime auth denial lacks resource scope and stable reason-code projection.

decision_assertions.asserts: Runtime auth event records allowed/denied decision, resource scope result, side-effect class, and stable deny reason without raw args.

rows.notes: Uses existing runtime auth policy event; operation identity tests cover pairing with tool invocation timelines.

forbidden_behaviors: Memory, RAG, LLM inference, or raw repository rows substitute for current business facts.
Permission denied leaks whether a business resource exists.
Stale, denied, invalid, or wrong-scope business facts enter action-bound paths.

decision_assertions.asserts: Trace/replay-safe projection proves BusinessFactRefV1/BusinessFactResultV1 tenant scope, resource version, freshness, source system, and fail-closed status.
Dev-contract forbidden-behavior gate covers stale and wrong-scope business facts before risk, approval, or action draft.

rows.notes: Current business fact coverage uses existing node/tool events plus payload/projection assertions; no new business_fact event type is added.

forbidden_behaviors: Candidate refs enter prompt, action, or replay authority without verification.
Invalid hash, invalid scope, stale, conflict, or no-evidence package creates action-bound recommendation.
Raw source blocks, OCR/parser metadata, or candidate text leaks through replay.

decision_assertions.asserts: RAG validation projection records verified, rejected, stale, conflict, invalid-hash, and invalid-scope refs without candidate-only authority.

rows.notes: RAG validation remains a node/retrieval event payload contract and should not create a parallel evidence event family.

forbidden_behaviors: Unsupported user-visible or action-bound claims enter risk, approval, or action draft.
Semantic review overrides deterministic hard gates for amount, time, negation, condition, or exception checks.
Business fact claims are proven by RAG or memory instead of scoped BusinessFactRefV1 authority.

decision_assertions.asserts: Claim verification bundle projection includes support status, hard-gate failures, safe support refs, blocked claims, and fail-closed route.

rows.notes: Claim verification coverage is asserted through existing claim_verify node completion payloads.

forbidden_behaviors: Risk gate routes unsupported, no-evidence, stale business fact, or invalid evidence scope into approval or action paths.
Approval-required or blocked decisions are owned by approval_gate instead of risk_gate.
Risk decision payload omits action payload hash, safety snapshot, business fact refs, or claim verification refs.

decision_assertions.asserts: Risk decision trace binds proposed action payload hash, business facts, verified evidence, claim bundle, safety snapshot, and final risk route before approval/action.
Dev-contract gate covers unsupported claims, no-evidence action recommendations, stale business facts, invalid evidence scope, and hash mismatch before action draft.

rows.notes: Risk decisions use the existing risk node event plus downstream approval/action refs; no risk-specific replay event type is added in this plan.

forbidden_behaviors: Ordinary chat creates approval decisions or trusted resume results.
Approval edit/respond/reject/ignore/expire paths execute old approval payloads.
Responded needs-info run is projected as completed or produces an action draft.

decision_assertions.asserts: Replay timelines cover requested, decided, expired, resumed, rejected, responded/needs-info, interrupted, and terminal status events with stable approval refs.

rows.notes: Approval lifecycle events already exist; Phase 35 timeline tests make their ordering and terminal semantics blocking.

forbidden_behaviors: Demo draft is represented as real external execution.
Action draft is created without target merchant, business facts, verified evidence, claim verification, risk decision, payload hash, or safety snapshot binding.
Raw proposed action payload or external side-effect details enter replay.

decision_assertions.asserts: Action draft replay payload carries draft id, payload hash, safety refs, demo execution mode, external_side_effect=false, and no raw action payload.
Replay timeline may include action_draft_created but must not include action_execution_completed in v1.9 demo mode.

rows.notes: Action draft coverage stays demo-only and explicitly excludes real external execution.
